research_notes: Blocked: teaching and legal employment are documented but full-time status and full appointment boundaries remain unavailable after employer post, first speech, local reporting and targeted employment/school searches.
The first speech's explicit full-time schoolteacher reference describes his mother, not Gregg. It is not evidence for his hours.
Do not assign Gabriel Ng's court or public-service roles from the joint employer post to Gregg. Unrelated sports and overseas namesakes were excluded.
Four-year board tenure, study and honorary student-association membership do not count toward employment headlines.

Follow-up2026-10-02: Youthlaw annual reports recover secretary observation2012–13 and departure13 November2016; governance remains excluded and not assumed paid. ABC identifies private as well as public/specialist school teaching, requiring employer-by-employer classification.

Searched university staff/course records, school history, association records and annual reports for legal and teaching boundaries. Public LinkedIn profile open returned (429) Too Many Requests; no retry in this cycle. Source-specific rate limit did not terminate research using other sources. Unrelated overseas trainer, engineer and lawyer namesakes excluded.

Follow-up2026-10-03: repeated exact-name searches across Thomson Geer, ANZUK Education, Victorian education, La Trobe course/staff material, legal judgments and Youthlaw annual reports. A contact-data aggregator displayed purported employer/date rows, but no primary employer record or accessible first-party professional profile corroborated those dates; they were not adopted. Youthlaw2013–14 and2014–15 reports only reconfirm secretary observations already bracketed by the2012–13 report and exact2016 cessation. No new employment boundary, hours or school identity established.

Next leads: school employment biography naming each institution and status; university appointment evidence; earlier law-firm employer and dates. Aggregated contact-profile claims are not adopted as employment evidence. Existing employer January2019 Slater and Gordon appointment retained; senior title does not prove full-time.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Reopened first-person23July2025speech and targeted Sale College, other Victorian schools, La Trobe2014appointments and earlier legal employer leads. Search engines returned generic institutional homepages and overseas athletics/loan-officer namesakes; no primary Thomson Geer/ANZUK employment confirmation. First-speech full-time teacher description refers to Gregg’s mother, not Gregg. Broad began-as-teacher election biography does not resolve earlier legal sequence. Employer January2019entry retained, school names/hours and law/university boundaries unknown.

Follow-up 5 October 2026: expanded exact-name searches to Matthew Gregg, earlier law-firm names, ANZUK, university teaching and DUSA office leads across both engines. Employer post still confirms January 2019 Slater and Gordon return, but no primary earlier-firm appointment, school-by-school contract or hours emerged. Irish law-journal editor, UK architecture researcher, US economist/aquaculture and sporting namesakes are not the Deakin MP; another DUSA presidents profile is not evidence for Gregg. Honorary student-association life membership does not establish a paid executive job. Existing Sale College 2016–2017 labels and Youthlaw secretary cessation remain supported, without invented leave or full-time intervals. Earlier legal and school boundaries require an individual employer or self-authored employment CV; repeated generic election biographies are exhausted. No numerical or research-status change.
